A Voice For Our Future
“Residents of the San Fernando Valley deserve a Member of Congress who will focus on their needs. I will fight to make sure every family has economic opportunity, protect Social Security and Medicare, and reduce the threat of climate change.”
## Meet Luz Rivas
Luz was raised in the Valley by a single mother. She earned a degree in Electrical Engineering from MIT and a Masters from Harvard.
Luz was elected to the State Assembly in 2018. She has focused on combatting climate change and improving access to math and science education.
Support Luz Today!
## Leader in the fight against Climate Change
“Rivas has been a consistent and unwavering champion for communities, public health, and bold climate action. She not only helped pass major climate legislation in 2022, but she also pushed to make these policies even stronger.”
- California Environmental Voters
## View Accomplishments
Luz in the News
Union nurses endorse Assemblymember Luz Maria Rivas for Congress
National Nurses United (NNU), the largest union of registered nurses in the United States, today announced they have endorsed Assemblymember Luz Maria Rivas to represent California’s 29th Congressional District, home to over 750,000 people in the San Fernando Valley of Los Angeles.
“We are proud to endorse Luz Maria Rivas in her race for Congress,” said Sandy Reding, RN, president of California Nurses Association (CNA) and vice president of NNU.
## View more
EMILYs List endorses Luz Rivas for Election to California’s 29th Congressional District
“Luz Maria Rivas has been a proven advocate for her community and an assemblywoman the people of her district can trust to deliver results and fight for their rights. EMILYs List is proud to endorse her for Congress because we know that she will continue that work in the U.S. House and help to achieve a Democratic pro-choice majority that will protect reproductive freedom in California and across the country. “
## View more
Mayor Karen Bass endorses Luz Rivas for Congress
“Luz Rivas has been a strong voice for us in Sacramento , including her role as leader of the L.A. delegation of the State Assembly, and she will continue to be our champion in Congress.” - Mayor Karen Bass

- Climate Change and Environment Secured funding to mitigate Extreme Heat and create the first heat wave ranking notification system in the nation. Jointly authored the Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act (SB54). Authored the first bill ever to require Climate Change education to be taught in CA public schools
- Education and Youth Created the first-ever California Youth Commission. Led legislation to ensure free school lunches. California became the first state to implement a statewide Universal Meals Program for school children. Advanced several dual language learner bills to identify early childhood DLLs and provide resources

## The Courage to Fight Back
Donald Trump and Republicans have driven up the costs for everything from groceries to healthcare. They sent ICE agents to brutalize local families. And they’re exposing us to harmful pollution in our air and water.
But Luz Rivas is fighting back . She doesn’t care if Trump and others attack her. She has the courage to stand up for us.
## Luz Fights for Us
She voted against the Trump bill that made massive cuts in health care .
She helped pass the law requiring Trump to release the Epstein files .
She has conducted oversight of ICE detention centers to expose Trump’s inhumane deportation program and has called to abolish ICE .
She secured $15 million in federal funding for higher education, infrastructure and public housing projects in the Valley.
We are strongly supporting
## Luz Rivas for Congress
Luz is the only candidate endorsed by teachers, labor unions, and Democrats!

pages.title: Luz Rivas for Congress
pages.text:
## $15 million in Federal Funding
Luz has secured $15 million in federal funding for projects in the Valley for 2026
Pacoima Wash Bridge Mitigation Project: $850,000 to improve safety, steel repairs, and fencing across six bridges.
CSUN Technology & STEM: Over $1,000,000 supporting the Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science (following prior state-level funding for the Autodesk Technology Engagement Center)
LA Fire Department Station in Sylmar: $850,000 for the construction of a new fire station in Sylmar
Panorama City / North Hills Infrastructure: $250,000 for ADA-compliant sidewalks, curbs, gutters, and crosswalks near Terra Bella Street and Wakefield Avenue.
Public Housing: $850,000 for energy-efficient cool roofs at San Fernando Gardens and $750,000 for Parthenia Place / computer lab and tech upgrades
LA Metro Bus Stop Upgrades: $660,000 for shade structures, bus stops, and public transit accessibility
Pacoima Warehouse Renovation: $968,000 for the Los Angeles County Fire Department to strengthen emergency response storage
